newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electric futures called lower, PV steady.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electric futures called lower, PV steady.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open steady to lower Tuesday following Monday's losses on easing cash prices and return of Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) in the western spot market.

In over-the-counter activity, May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $13.00-13.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Monday's settlement at $13.43, and May Palo Verde (PV) at $17.50-17.75 versus Monday's close of $17.48.
The May contracts are set to expire Friday.

While the PV half of the complex is expected to receive support by fairly hot weather in the Southwest and southern California, it faces downward pressure from falling natural gas futures, market sources said.
May Henry Hub natgas futures opened Tuesday down 2.4 cents at $2.040 per million British thermal units.

Spring fish flush at the hydroelectric dams on the Columbia River began yesterday after spillage on the Snake River started about two weeks ago. The spillage on both rivers is said to cut the amount of surplus power in the Northwest.
Unplanned outages continued to plagued the West. Pacific Gas and Electric Co shut Monday a 330 megawatt (MW) unit at its natural gas-fired generating complex in Pittsburg, Calif.
A 750 MW unit 1 at the coal-fired Navajo power plant near Page, Arizona, was shut this past weekend for unplanned repairs, and expected to resume operation by Wednesday.
A 300 MW unit at the San Juan coal-fired station in New Mexico was also taken offline over the weekend for repairs.

Besides those outages, about 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was already out of service in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance, as well as hydropower displacement sales, but some of the capacity is expected to return to service later this week.

Moreover, three large nuclear power units in the West are currently shut for refueling and maintenance: the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 in Avila Beach, California, 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in San Clemente, Calif., and 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Richland, Washington.

Meterologists expected temperatures throughout the Northwest would vary widely, averaging about five degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the extreme northwest to as much as seven degrees F below normal in the extreme northeast.

In the Southwest, readings would run from four degrees F above normal in the far west to seven degrees F below normal in th extreme east. Spring snow may continue to fall in the Central Rockies, forecasters said.
